fixes.explanation: Not quite, baker. The text says, “Now Jericho was tightly shut up because of the Israelites. No one went out and no one came in.” (Joshua 6:1) That's a city sealed up tight. It's like a bakery with the doors locked, the blinds down, and the sign flipped to CLOSED. Nobody's strolling in, and nobody's strolling out.

Yes. The text says, “So he had the ark of the LORD carried around the city, circling it once. And the people returned to the camp and spent the night there.” (Joshua 6:11) One lap, then back to camp for the night. Then they got up and did it again the next day. That's some serious patience, and I know how hard waiting is. I once waited in a junk drawer for years.

Tamar's a real name in the Bible, baker, but she's not in this story. Joshua says, “Only Rahab the prostitute and all those with her in her house will live, because she hid the spies we sent.” (Joshua 6:17) Rahab is the one who hid the spies, and that's the reason the text gives. Her house is the one that gets spared.

Deborah shows up later in the Bible as a judge, but she has no part in Jericho. Listen to who Joshua names: Rahab, the woman who hid the spies. Her whole household was spared, “all those with her in her house.” (Joshua 6:17) That's a lot of people covered by one brave choice.
